title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: TONY'S DRIVEWAY
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Tony, an elevator repairman in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
Tony shared a driveway with his neighbor Dolores, who was seventy-six.
For two years, they had not said one nice word to each other.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE LEAVES
segments.quote: When angry, count ten, before you speak; if very angry, an hundred.
segments.author: Thomas Jefferson
lines: Every fall, Dolores blew her leaves onto Tony's side. Tony blew them back.
One Saturday, he marched over to yell. Then he remembered a line from Thomas Jefferson.
When angry, count ten, before you speak; if very angry, an hundred.
Tony counted. He got to sixty-three, and went back inside.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE BOAT
segments.quote: Don't throw stones at your neighbors if your own windows are glass.
segments.author: Benjamin Franklin
lines: On Monday, he complained about Dolores to his crew all through lunch.
His partner Ray asked one question. Tony, how long has your rusty boat been parked across that driveway?
Three years. Ray grinned and quoted Ben Franklin.
Don't throw stones at your neighbors if your own windows are glass.
That weekend, Tony sold the boat.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE LADDER
segments.quote: Men exist for the sake of one another. Teach them then or bear with them.
segments.author: Marcus Aurelius
lines: In November, Tony fell off a ladder. Broken ankle. No driving for six weeks.
Next morning, Dolores honked from her old Buick. Get in.
Tony almost said no. Then he thought of Marcus Aurelius, the Roman emperor:
Men exist for the sake of one another. Teach them then or bear with them.
So he got in, and bore with her driving. She takes corners like a getaway driver.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BLOWER
segments.quote: The best way to cheer yourself is to try to cheer somebody else up.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: On those rides, Tony learned the leaf blower was her late husband's. She never learned to aim it.
Stuck on his couch, Tony felt gloomy. Then he read the Mark Twain line on his coffee mug.
The best way to cheer yourself is to try to cheer somebody else up.
So he sat in a lawn chair and coached her. By sundown, every leaf was in a bag.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE WORKBENCH
segments.quote: No one is useless in this world who lightens the burden of it for any one else.
segments.author: Charles Dickens
lines: Still, Tony felt useless. A repairman who couldn't climb a stair.
So Dolores brought over a broken lamp, a dead clock, and a line from Charles Dickens.
No one is useless in this world who lightens the burden of it for any one else.
Tony fixed both from a stool. Then he asked what else was broken.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE KEY
segments.quote: We do not so much need the help of our friends as the confidence of their help in need.
segments.author: Epicurus
lines: By spring, Tony was walking again, and the rides were over. Dolores got quiet.
So Tony gave her a key to his garage, with a note from Epicurus, the Greek thinker:
We do not so much need the help of our friends as the confidence of their help in need.
Now they share the driveway, the leaves, and every Steelers game.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Count to ten. Fix your own yard. Accept help. Cheer someone up. Lighten a load. Be there.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Count before you speak. Fix your own yard first. Accept the ride. Cheer someone up. Lighten a load. And be there.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night. And if your neighbor drives a Buick, buckle up.
